properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: This is the app's entire outbound API surface (market data, translations, AI providers, exports, newsletters, orderbooks, trading adapters, Nostr relays). None of the 106 sites configures ciphers or groups — the posture is set by the Node 22 runtime, so the remediation is runtime-level (Node 22+ can offer X25519MLKEM768 via tls default groups / OpenSSL config) and needs peer support; call sites need no code change. Changeable here at the deployment level, not per call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 is this codebase's workhorse hash: content addressing (content-addressable.ts, IPFS route), Nostr event IDs (nostr/route.ts:183), email-verification token hashing, API-key verifiers (api-keys.ts, gateway/api-key.ts:197 — note: unsalted SHA-256 over plaintext keys used as a verifier), export checksums, request fingerprints, cache keys. All 21 packages show live createHash('sha256')/subtle.digest('SHA-256') chains; quantum-relevant only via Grover (A-).

properties.name: pqs:context

HMAC-SHA-256 remains sound classically; Grover-halved against a quantum attacker.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RFC 8291 Web Push key schedule: HKDF-SHA-256 derives the PRK from the auth secret, then the CEK (128 bits) and nonce (96 bits) for aes128gcm — protocol-fixed parameters, changeable only by the Web Push standard.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Web Push payload encryption (RFC 8188 aes128gcm): HKDF-derived CEK/nonce, subtle.encrypt AES-GCM with 128-bit tag — the pushed content is confidential only under AES-GCM + an ECDH-P256-derived key, both recorded as separate objects.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-128 is fixed by the Web Push aes128gcm content coding (128-bit CEK) — quantum-resistant in practice (Grover halves to 64-bit margin) but below CNSA 2.0's AES-256 requirement; not changeable unilaterally, it is protocol-fixed.
